item.description: Dec 5, 2025; Houston, Texas, USA; Phoenix Suns guard Collin Gillespie (12) dribbles the ball during the fourth quarter against the Houston Rockets at Toyota Center. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images NEW ORLEANS — It wasn’t just another hard-fought victory; it was a character-building win for the Phoenix Suns. They are beginning to discover something important about themselves: they can win games even when things aren’t going according to plan. Phoenix escaped New Orleans with a 121-117 overtime win Monday night, extending its winning streak to four. However, the result required considerably more effort than expected against a struggling, shorthanded Pelicans team. Dec 27, 2025; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; Phoenix Suns guard Devin Booker (1) dribbles against New Orleans Pelicans guard/forward Micah Peavy (14) during the second half at Smoothie King Center. Devin Booker appeared ready to deliver the decisive moment late in regulation, connecting on a midrange jumper. But New Orleans answered again. Booker subsequently lost possession under pressure from Herb Jones on Phoenix’s final opportunity, sending the game into overtime after a desperation attempt at the buzzer fell short. With Phoenix still searching for consistent answers at point guard, his ability to organize possessions and contribute when the game tightens becomes increasingly valuable. Jalen Green also brought a noticeable intensity, while Phoenix became more physical defensively. Booker even battled Zion Williamson for loose balls, illustrating a team that wasn’t willing to surrender another opportunity. Although the Bronx Bombers shifted Gil to the bullpen at the back end of last season, Tigers manager AJ Hinch will reportedly give the player a chance to make the rotation out of spring training. Here is how Gil will fit into the Tigers organization. Luis Gil Could Be Major Bargain for Detroit Tigers Detroit already looks to have a good amount of depth at starting pitcher. Framber Valdez still has two more seasons to go on his mammoth free agent contract , while the team recently extended the promising Troy Melton to a six-year deal . item.title: Everything Dan Lanning said before Oregon hosts Washington
item.description: The Oregon Ducks have come a long way during their four-game winning streak. From seemingly impossible playoff odds to having the inside track to the Big Ten title game, everything is at stake this Saturday night in the regular-season finale against the Washington Huskies . The Ducks picked up a big win at Michigan State on a short week and head into the final game of the season at Autzen Stadium with the potential to win their way into the conference championship game and secure a spot in the College Football Playoff. Dan Lanning didn't waste time shifting focus to Washington, as it's a rivalry game Oregon never takes lightly. Washington knocked off Indiana in overtime last week in Seattle, clearing a path for Oregon to reach Indianapolis and the Big Ten Championship Game . The Huskies , not unlike the Ducks, have hit their stride on offense in recent weeks and have some momentum heading into Eugene. Lanning detailed his thoughts on the upcoming matchup, as well as the status of several key injuries and Oregon's conference title and playoff hopes heading into Senior Day at Autzen Stadium. Here's everything Lanning had to say at his weekly press conference on Monday night before Oregon hosts Washington. Opening Statement Dan Lanning: "Obviously an exciting opportunity for us this weekend. Get an opportunity to play a rival and our seniors' last game here potentially in Autzen. So exciting for them, especially for the guys that have given so much to this program and been involved for as long as they have. And for it to be a game like this one is a special opportunity for us. Washington's coming off a big win against Indiana and played extremely well, had as many yards as anybody has against that team this year, and it seems like things are really clicking for them. So I think both of us are on the uptick, and they've been as good as anybody. This season on the road, and certainly in the fourth quarter, they've gotten better and better. So, a really good opportunity for our fans to show up and make our atmosphere really special, and celebrate these seniors as we get an opportunity to compete." Maintaining Focus Question: You always talk about trying to not make the moment bigger than it is, but senior day, huge rivalry, the postseason implications; how do you reiterate to your team to take this one day at a time and not focus on making it too big? DL: "Yeah, just remind them of reality. It wasn't that long ago that we were kind of thrown to the curb, and that's all changed because they were able to focus on what's right in front of them. item.title: Islanders blow two-goal lead in embarassing loss that gave Maple Leafs first win this month
item.description: Toronto Maple Leafs center Dakota Joshua reacts after scoring a goal against the New York Islanders on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, at UBS Arena in Elmont, N.Y. There is only so bad a loss can be in the NHL before Thanksgiving, but the Islanders got pretty close to the limit Monday night. Not only did they blow a two-goal lead on home ice to woeful Maple Leafs side that took its first victory in the month of November, 4-2 after losing nine in a row, but the Islanders lost top-line winger Kyle Palmieri to injury as well. Just as the Islanders were getting healthy — and after the Maple Leafs looked utterly hapless through the first 20 minutes of this game — it was a brutal 1-2 punch. Toronto Maple Leafs center Dakota Joshua reacts after scoring a goal against the New York Islanders on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, at UBS Arena in Elmont, N.Y. Robert Sabo for NY Post Palmieri exited early in the second period when his right leg wrapped around the Leafs’ goal post while he was colliding with Easton Cowan. Having torn his left ACL last year, Palmieri didn’t put weight on his right skate while coming off the ice, and walked up the tunnel under his own power. The Islanders declared him out for the rest of the night with a lower-body injury. In the immediate aftermath, they didn’t look too deterred, with Mathew Barzal scoring a highlight-reel goal to open his account for the season. His curl up the wall and subsequent dance through William Nylander and Aatu Raty before scoring to put the Islanders up 2-0 6:55 into the second was vintage stuff — a burst of inspiration and individual creativity that few players around the league are capable of. It was also the last good moment the Islanders would have on a night that, to that point, had looked fairly straightforward. The two teams seemed to do a body swap. item.description: Nov 23, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) passes the ball against the Portland Trail Blazers during the second quarter at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images On the back of a 132-129 win over the Milwaukee Bucks , the Philadelphia 76ers had extended their winning streak to five games, boasting considerable momentum entering Monday night’s matchup. Unfortunately, things did not play out well for Philadelphia, as the Portland Trail Blazers snapped their winning streak in a blowout 128-111 victory. The 76ers simply looked outmatched on Monday night. Although the performances from the superstar trio of LeBron James (23 PTS, 6 REB, 3 AST), Tyrese Maxey (22 PTS, 5 AST), and Jaylen Brown (20 PTS, 4 AST, 2 STL) were noteworthy, they were not enough to contain the offensive barrage from Deni Avdija and Damian Lillard , who combined for 49 points. With this loss, Philadelphia finds itself falling to 14-4 on the season. While this sees them retain their place at the top of the Eastern Conference leaderboard, some points from Monday night’s performance may need addressing to prevent a potential losing slide. On that note, here are four reasons the 76ers failed to secure the win against the Trail Blazers. The Lack Of A True Big Man Was Evident One of the factors that stood out during Monday night’s game was the impact of the big man. With Joel Embiid sidelined , the Philadelphia 76ers opted to start Jabari Walker at center, allowing Dean Wade to come off the bench. In principle, this has proven to be a solid tactic because of Walker’s athleticism, versatility, and hustle. Unfortunately, against Blazers center Donovan Clingan , this wasn’t the case. Although Walker did a solid job, posting 10 points and five rebounds for the game, he was clearly outplayed by his positional matchup. To that end, when considering that Clingan notched 15 points and 18 rebounds for the game, the Blazers center single-handedly dominated on the glass, helping Portland win the rebounding battle 49-33. While the small-ball approach has merit, against a team with an established center like the Blazers, Philadelphia found itself struggling. Given that the repercussions were felt more tangibly in the second half, the 76ers’ need for a true center in the rotation in such situations is evident. item.description: IMAGO / Marty Jean Louis ©Credit - Imago The drama surrounding the Sunday night match-up between Warriors and Celtics doesn’t seem to end. Even after a day, the refs came back with a jab aimed at the Dubs. Today, Steve Kerr has made his frustration with NBA flopping increasingly clear this season, even suggesting that the Warriors may have to adopt the same tactics to keep up with their opponents. But the comments took an ironic turn. Just hours after the Warriors coach joked about teaching defenders to exaggerate contact, the NBA announced a fine for one of his own players. The league fined backup guard Will Richard $2,000 for flopping during Sunday’s 88–87 victory over the Boston Celtics. The violation occurred with 8:47 remaining in the second quarter, when Richard was defending Payton Pritchard, coming off a screen set by Neemias Quetta. No one noticed it then. Kerr's anti flopping crusade just backfired spectacularly. Subscribe for the NBA drama and coaching contradictions you won't see coming. However, the NBA announced the penalty roughly two hours after Kerr addressed reporters following practice. It created an awkward coincidence for a coach who had just spoken out against the very behavior that got his player fined. “I think we probably have to start teaching our defensive players to flop on screens because everybody around the league is doing it,” Kerr said. “You know, you set a screen and guys chase around the screen and act like they’ve been hit by a car, and the whole bench jumps up. And those are automatic fouls. So we’ve got to start teaching that.” Kerr also argued that the league could eliminate the problem by enforcing its rules more consistently. “I’ve said this many times. Just eliminate the (expletive), and the players will stop doing it. But they don’t eliminate it, and so players keep doing it.” Warriors’ guard Richard’s fine came after the league reviewed his defensive sequence against Pritchard. The Celtics guard drove toward the paint and attempted a shot off the glass, while Richard appeared to exaggerate the contact and go to the floor. Pritchard missed, and Georges Niang collected the rebound. The officials did not penalize Richard during the game, leaving the league office to assess the play afterward. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.) Player development has suffered: United has no representation on the curren
